headline: Yala & Bundala: Leopard Dens, Untamed Scrublands & Lagoon Aviaries
description:
Yala’s rocky outcrops, palu trees and coastal dunes shelter one of the densest leopard populations anywhere, alongside sloth bears, elephants, crocodiles and more than two hundred bird species. Next door, Bundala’s salt pans and lagoons are a winter home for flamingos and migratory waders.

I work with a senior tracker who reads alarm calls and pug marks rather than radio chatter, and we favour the quieter blocks and corridors so that a sighting means stillness — engine off — not a traffic jam.

quickFacts.label: Best Sighting Window
quickFacts.note: Low water levels draw leopards and elephants to the waterholes

quickFacts.label: Annual Rest Period
quickFacts.note: Block 1 usually closes for a few weeks; Block 5 and Bundala stay open

quickFacts.label: Suggested Stay
quickFacts.note: A dusk drive, a full dawn drive and an unhurried camp afternoon

quickFacts.label: Private Access Route
quickFacts.note: Or about 3 hrs from Galle Fort along the coast

guideNote.heading: Why My Safaris Start Where the Jeeps Don’t
paragraphs: Block 1 at 06:00 can feel like a car park. We often enter through quieter gates, follow the tracker’s instinct along the elephant corridors and wait — engine off, voices low — at a waterhole he trusts. The reward is a leopard that walks past on its own terms.

experiences.title: Private Leopard Tracking with a Senior Tracker
experiences.text: A modified open 4x4 for your party only, packed breakfast under a tamarind tree and the patience to wait where the tracks are freshest.

image.alt: Male leopard walking a red dirt trail in Yala National Park

experiences.title: Block 5 & the Lunugamvehera Elephant Corridor
experiences.text: Fewer vehicles, wilder country: riverine forest, rock pools and the corridor elephants use to move between parks.

image.alt: Safari vehicle crossing a dry riverbed in Yala as a naturalist scans for tracks

experiences.title: Bundala Salt Pans & Migratory Flamingos
experiences.text: Between November and March the lagoons fill with greater flamingos, painted storks and visiting waders. Binoculars and a telephoto lens are in the vehicle.

fieldNotes.title: Engine-Off Protocol
fieldNotes.text: At every sighting we switch off and keep our distance. If a jam forms, we leave — the animal’s comfort comes first.

fieldNotes.title: Neutral Colours
fieldNotes.text: Khaki, olive and sand tones are best. Bright white and red stand out against the scrub and unsettle wildlife.

fieldNotes.title: Patience Pays
fieldNotes.text: Leopards are most active in the first two hours of light. The longest waits have given my guests their finest sightings.

tours.title: The Grand Ceylon Odyssey
tours.summary: The quintessential Ceylon masterpiece. Climb Sigiriya at sunrise before the heat, wander sacred tooth relic temples, traverse the tea mountains on the vintage observation train, and track leopards in Yala.

cover.alt: Tea train crossing the Nine Arch Bridge in Ella in morning light

tours.title: Wild Leopards & Untamed Coastlines
tours.summary: Immersive expedition for wildlife photographers and conservation enthusiasts. Private trackers, custom open-sided 4x4 safaris, and private coastal yacht charters for sperm and blue whale sightings.
